# 2025 Lexus ES: KBB Expert Review Summary

## Review Details
- **Author:** Colin Ryan
- **Updated:** January 30, 2025
- **Expert rating:** 4.7 (consumer rating: 4.2, based on 70 reviews)
- **Pros:** Smooth ride, attractive pricing, roomy cabin
- **Cons:** All-wheel drive is only available with the base engine

## Expert Commentary

- **Engine/hybrid performance:** The ES 350's 3.5-liter V6 makes 302 hp and reaches 60 mph in 6.6 seconds. The ES 300h's 215 hp is "not especially impressive." The review gives the ES 250 an 8.1-second 0-60 time, but the spec table lists 8.6 seconds.
- **Fuel economy:** The ES 300h is rated at 44 mpg combined. The ES 350 is rated at 26 mpg and the ES 250 at 28 mpg. The reviewer says gasoline models are "more tolerable than remarkable." Regular fuel is acceptable for all variants.
- **Ride/handling:** The ride is smooth and comfort-oriented. The reviewer would skip the F Sport Handling option, which adds an adaptive suspension.
- **Quietness:** Not stated.
- **Interior design/materials:** The cabin is calm and spacious with quality materials. F Sport aluminum accents draw on traditional Japanese swords.
- **Seats and rear space:** Rear legroom is 39.2 inches, and the rear seatbacks are angled to improve headroom. The rear seats do not split or fold.
- **Trunk:** The review cites 16.7 cubic feet, but the spec table lists 13.9 cubic feet.
- **Infotainment/touchscreen/touchpad:** The review mentions a 12.3-inch touchscreen only in the Black Line Special Edition, and says these items are also available in other ES models. No touchpad is mentioned.
- **Smartphone integration:** Wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto is standard across the lineup. Wired connection is not discussed.
- **Driver assistance:** The review mentions forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking, pedestrian detection, and lane-centering assistance as standard. Adaptive cruise control is standard, works at all speeds, and adds lane tracing. "Lexus Safety System+" is not named.
- **Value:** The review calls the ES relatively affordable for a luxury sedan, notes strong resale value, and says most buyers pay less than sticker price.
- **BMW 5 Series comparison:** Not mentioned.

## Equipment Facts

- **Screen size:** 12.3-inch touchscreen (Black Line Special Edition; available in other ES models)
- **Head-up display:** Included in the Black Line Special Edition; available in other ES models
- **Physical climate controls:** Not stated
- **Voice assistant:** A "Voice Recognition System" appears in the feature list; no details given
- **OTA updates:** Not stated
- **Digital key:** Not stated. The Black Line package includes a "SmartAccess Card Key," and the spec list includes "Proximity Sensing Keyless Entry"
- **Hands-free driving:** Not stated
- **Automated parking:** Not stated
- **Ventilated seats:** Heated and ventilated front seats are part of the optional Premium package
- **Massage seats:** Not stated
- **Rear seat features:** A powered rear shade is standard on the Luxury model
- **Adaptive/air suspension:** Adaptive suspension is part of F Sport Handling on the ES 350 and ES 300h. No air suspension is mentioned.
- **Rear-wheel steering:** Not stated
- **Rear legroom:** 39.2 inches
- **Trunk volume:** 16.7 cu ft per the review; 13.9 cu ft per the spec table
- **Mark Levinson audio:** Available in the Luxury and Ultra Luxury models, with 1,800 watts through 17 speakers
- **Moonroof/panoramic roof:** A panoramic moonroof is optional on the ES 350

## 1. KBB Expert Review

- **Author/date:** Eric Brandt, Managing Editor; updated May 27, 2026
- **Expert rating:** 4.2
- **Pros:** Hybrid and EV options, high-tech interior, class-leading resale value
- **Cons:** Tame performance, some odd interior materials

**Performance and efficiency**
- The hybrid ES 350h (244 hp) is described as predictable, with efficiency prioritized over performance. Lexus estimates up to 46 combined mpg.
- The hybrid is noisy under hard acceleration but adequate for relaxed daily driving.
- The single-motor EV (ES 350e) has less power but more torque than the hybrid, with similar overall performance.
- The dual-motor ES 500e is the quickest model but is still tame compared with rivals. The review calls it a laid-back sedan.

**Range and charging:** The page gives up to 307 miles (350e) and 276 miles (500e), plus an 8-hour 240V charge time. The review does not discuss DC fast charging.

**Ride, handling, and quietness:** The review says the hybrid rides pleasantly. The EVs are noted as free of the hybrid's engine noise. Handling is not discussed in depth.

**Interior and materials**
- Soft-touch materials are abundant, but some feel odd. The synthetic suede on the steering wheel is singled out, and buyers wanting a traditional luxury feel may prefer real leather.
- Front seats are roomy, even for taller drivers.
- Rear seats are described as adult-friendly, with 40.7 inches of rear legroom (1.5 inches more than the outgoing ES).

**Trunk:** The review says the hybrid has 17.4 cu ft and the EV has about one more cubic foot. This conflicts with the page's specs (13.3 cu ft cargo; 18.2 cu ft in the styles table for the hybrid).

**Infotainment and controls:** The review praises the new infotainment system's crisper resolution and home button, and it notes standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. It says the tactile HVAC bar and roller volume dial are easy to use.

**Driver assistance:** Not discussed in the review.

**Value**
- The hybrid has a lower starting price than the EV and is called a uniquely good value in the class.
- The ES has class-leading resale value, and the reviewer expects the hybrid to hold value better than the EV.
- Pricing is inconsistent: the lead says $48,795 and the pricing section says $48,895.

**Comparisons:** No explicit comparison to the BMW 5 Series. The review says the BMW i5 and Mercedes-Benz EQE Sedan both start in the high $60k range.

**Short answer:** The 2019 ES 350 F Sport used a touchpad controller that most reviewers disliked. For 2022, Lexus added a touchscreen but kept the touchpad.

**2019 model**
- An Autoblog quick spin called the Remote Touch touchpad a serious drawback and said it could be a dealbreaker in a daily driver. You also have to deal with the Remote Touch interface and its abysmal touchpad controller.
- Motor1 said the touchpad made on-screen selections confusing while driving, because the driver must first look at the screen to confirm the cursor's initial location before using the touchpad to highlight the desired on-screen button.
- Autoguide was more forgiving, describing the trackpad as relatively easy to use, though further simplifying things Apple CarPlay is also baked in.

**2022 model**
- The headline change was a touchscreen. Cars.com noted that the 2022 ES has kept its touchpad controller, its best upgrade is a new touchscreen to replace the previous non-touch display.
- Cars.com also said the old touchpad was truly hard to use while driving, requiring more steps than simply touching a screen, and it was inconsistent in its movement and activation.
- Autoblog's 2023 review, which covers the 2022 refresh, said the touchscreen is faster (and safer) than scrolling on the touchpad.
- Cars.com's tester noted that the touchpad is sticking around for now, so it remains available for drivers who prefer it.

**Owner views:** Consumer opinions are mixed. One 2020 ES owner on Cars.com said they liked the touchpad because it keeps the screen free of fingerprints, while another wished the car had a touchscreen. The safety systems are lovely, I really like the Lexus touch pad, I love seeing my screen on a sunny day finger print free!!

This was a single search, and the 2019 coverage is older (the Autoblog piece dates from December 2018). Check current reviews before deciding.

**Author and date:** Matt Schmitz, February 14, 2022 (Cars.com).

**Trim tested:** The article focuses on the six-cylinder ES 350, with its 302-horsepower V-6 and standard suspension. It compares this against the four-cylinder ES 250 and mentions the optional F Sport package. It does not name a generation number.

**Things the reviewer likes:**
- **Touchscreen:** A 12.3-inch touchscreen replaces the old non-touch display, which the article calls hard to use while driving. The touchpad controller remains available.
- **Apple CarPlay:** It can use the full 12.3-inch screen.
- **Screen position:** The display sits 4.3 inches closer to the driver, within arm's reach.
- **Ride (standard suspension):** The base suspension with the V-6 provides confidence, comfort, and refinement off the line and at speed.
- **Safety:** Lexus Safety System Plus 2.5 adds standard blind spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert. Intersection Turning Assist and Curve Speed Reduction are also included.
- **Price and availability:** The ES 350 has the same starting price as the ES 250, $41,875 including destination. Per Cars.com inventory figures, it is also easier to find.

**Things the reviewer doesn't like:**
- **Camera quality:** The backup and 360-degree cameras distort images and are less clear than they should be. The main screen's graphics are praised.
- **Lane centering:** The system keeps a consistent lane position inconsistently, tending to drift toward the right side.
- **F Sport package:** It has a harsher ride and unique suspension tuning, even with optional adjustable shocks. The reviewer says its handling gains aren't worth the cost. The article describes it as a "sleek, attractive package" mainly for looks.
- **Front-wheel drive:** The ES 350 is FWD only. The article argues the V-6 could use the traction of AWD, which is only offered on the ES 250.

**BMW / 5 Series comparison:** The article makes no comparison to BMW or the 5 Series.

**Not covered:** The article doesn't address quietness, seats, rear-seat space, trunk, fuel economy, or engine/transmission details beyond the horsepower figure and drivetrain layout.

I found plenty of CT5 vs. 5 Series comparisons, but nearly all come from dealership blogs or spec-comparison sites. I didn't find a formal head-to-head group test from a major magazine. The points below combine independent CT5 reviews with comparison pages that cite magazine test data.

**Independent CT5 reviews**
- **Consumer Reports:** Its road test praises the ride and handling but says the powertrain lacks polish. It also says the four-cylinder trails upscale rivals on acceleration and fuel economy, and that rear-seat entry and headroom are limited. We found that it has a dynamic ride and handling combination that should impress those who like driving, but its powertrain lacks polish. Empirically, acceleration and fuel economy are not on par with its upscale peers.
- **The Car Connection (dated September 30, 2026):** It likes the engaging handling and strong safety kit, but flags a coarse base engine and a busy infotainment layout. The turbocharged four-cylinder feels strained under heavy throttle and sounds unusually wheezy for a luxury sedan.
- **Autoblog:** It says some interior materials fall short of European luxury benchmarks, but rear-seat space exceeds that of the BMW 3 Series and Alfa Romeo Giulia... Cargo space, however, is rather poor.
- **TrueCar:** Its review benchmarks the CT5 against the 3 Series rather than the 5 Series, so treat it as background only.

**Head-to-head points against the 5 Series**
- **Entry engine (530i):** A Lithia dealer page citing Car and Driver says the Cadillac CT5 turbo V6 is faster than the 530i 2.0 turbo 4-cylinder hybrid. A BMW dealer page citing Motor Trend reaches the opposite conclusion about the base CT5, saying the 530i is quicker than the CT5's four-cylinder.
- **Upper engine (540i):** BMW's 540i makes 40 more horsepower (375 vs. 335) than the CT5's optional 3.0 turbo V6. The CT5's V6, however, produces 7 lbs.-ft. more torque (405 vs. 398) than the 540i xDrive's standard 3.0 turbo 6-cylinder.
- **Weight and size:** Lithia argues the CT5 weighs about 400 to 550 pounds less than the BMW 5 Series and is 5.4 inches shorter, which it says helps handling.
- **Chassis tech:** BMW's comparison notes the 5 Series offers an available adjustable active suspension system... Cadillac doesn't offer an active suspension on the CT5.
- **Braking:** A BMW-hosted page citing Car and Driver's testing says the 5 Series stops much shorter than the CT5, at 156 feet versus 169 feet from 70 mph.
- **Efficiency:** Figures conflict. TrueCar lists the 5 Series at 29 MPG in the city and 35 MPG on the highway, versus 22 MPG in the city and 31 MPG on the highway for the CT5. Crestview lists the CT5 at 23/33 and the 540i at 26/33.
- **Cargo:** BMW's comparison says the 5 Series has a much larger trunk than the CT5 (18.4 vs. 11.9 cubic feet).
- **Space:** Cabled Ahmer reports more front and rear legroom for the CT5, while BMW's own page gives the 5 Series a little more front headroom and shoulder room.
- **Infotainment:** Cabled Ahmer contrasts the CT5's massive 33-inch diagonal LED display with the 14.9-inch 5 Series screen, while The Car Connection calls the CT5's wide display crowded.
- **Price:** TrueCar lists the BMW 5 Series is more expensive with a starting MSRP of $61,950, versus $50,995 for the CT5. Cabled Ahmer gives CT5-V $60,095 and 540i xDrive $67,700.

**Caveats**
- **Dealer bias:** Most comparison pages come from dealerships, and each tends to favor its own brand.
- **Conflicting specs:** Roadlancer describes a 10-inch infotainment display on the 2026 CT5, while TrueCar describes a 33-inch curved display combining the digital cluster and infotainment screen.
- **Reliability is mixed:** Survey results differ by year and source. Consumer Reports ranks BMW third in overall reliability. Cadillac is ranked 17th. That data is from early 2023, and a BMW dealer page cites a 2024 J.D. Power study favoring BMW.
- **Dated comparisons:** Capital One's comparison is from 2023, before the CT5's 2025 redesign.

**Bottom line:** Against the 530i, the CT5 is generally cheaper and has more tech and legroom, while the BMW tends to win on efficiency, cargo, braking, and chassis hardware. Against the 540i, BMW has the power edge on paper, and the CT5 V6 is the closer rival on price. For a definitive answer, I'd check original Car and Driver, Motor Trend, or Edmunds tests for the specific model years you're considering. I can search for those next.

I found mostly anecdotal forum reports, plus a few ratings and reviews. Many "2.5T" threads on these forums are about the GV80 SUV, so I focused on G80 threads. The search results don't give reliable dates for most threads, and forum posts skew toward problems, so treat these as individual experiences rather than a reliability measure.

**Recurring complaints in G80 2.5T threads**

- **Battery drain:** A 2021 2.5T AWD Prestige owner said the battery went dead unless the car was driven daily, requiring two jump starts in a week. Battery is going dead if car not started daily. 2 trips to jump the car by Genesis/AAA this week. Another member suggested the battery might be the root cause of the electrical issues and urged the owner to push the dealer for a replacement (a full charge test, then a battery replacement if it appears to be the culprit).
- **Steering drift:** A 2021 G80 2.5T RWD owner described the car drifting left and right at highway speeds, requiring constant small corrections. There is an issue with the steering on a 2021 Genesis G80 2.5t. This is most noticeable at highway speeds, but the car never seems to stay straight. That thread is dated March 2024. The same owner later bought a 2008 Lexus RX350 as a daily driver, citing the G80's mileage and wanting something more dependable (considering the amount of miles put on the G80).
- **Infotainment:** One owner's head unit repeatedly froze and restarted. The dealer found error codes pointing to a bad head unit, and it was replaced (codes indicating a bad head unit, and a replacement head unit arrived). The thread doesn't specify the engine.
- **Warning lights:** A 2021 2.5T AWD Prestige owner had a check engine light come on an hour after purchase and return on a short drive. The dealer initially found nothing wrong, then pointed to the engine control system (the light came on one hour after purchase, and the dealer said everything was fine).
- **Transmission and power:** In another G80 owner's log, the car surged under hard acceleration, and the transmission downshifted too early after about 12,000 miles. The dealer reset the ECU, and the behavior returned months later (the dealer reset the ECU, and the transmission worked for a couple more months before going back to the poor shift strategy). The engine isn't specified.
- **Stop-start:** Owners disliked the auto stop-start. One said it feels like the car will stall on restart and asked how to disable it permanently (the restart feels like a stall, and the poster asked how to disable it permanently). A Miami owner also found the shutoff annoying with the AC running (the engine auto shutoff is annoying, especially in Miami heat when the AC compressor shuts off at a light).

**Positive and mixed long-term reports**

- A 2021 2.5T Prestige owner reported no problems after about a year and 10,000 miles, with seat firmness as the only complaint (one year, 10,000 miles, and no problems, with the driver's seat bottom as the only dislike).
- Another 2.5T owner reported about 30 mpg over more than 9,000 miles, mostly highway driving, and said the 4-cylinder has been great (an overall average of 30 mpg at just over 9,000 miles, with about 65–70% non-city driving).
- Fuel economy reports conflict. One owner averaged 15.7 MPG, but that person made almost all trips under 20 miles (mostly short trips under 20 miles, with an average of 15.7 MPG).
- The longest-running 2.5T thread I found reached about 53,000 miles (owned for some time, bought in January 2021, now at 53k miles).

**Independent ratings and reviews**

- Verified owner reviews on SureCritic are generally positive. One reviewer called the G80 a very reliable vehicle since in 2 years no issues, though another mentioned a battery failure and wind and creaking noise (the battery failure, wind noise, and creaking are annoying but acceptable).
- Ratings disagree. CarGurus says the second generation earned Great scores in 2023 and 2024, but Average in 2025 and 2026. CarsCounsel gives the 2021 model an 86 out of 100 reliability rating from J.D. Power, while Carbuzz lists 2021 as N/A. iSeeCars gives the G80 a reliability score of 5.9 out of 10.
- CarsCounsel also says this generation faced fuel pump failures affecting 2021-2023 models and instrument panel display issues in 2023-2024 vehicles. I didn't verify these against NHTSA, so if you're considering a specific car, check its VIN for open recalls.

**Bottom line:** The G80 2.5T threads show a mix of battery, electrical, stop-start, and steering complaints, alongside owners who report few or no problems. The results don't include many high-mileage 2.5T reports, so long-term durability is still uncertain. If you want, I can search for GV80 threads separately or look for NHTSA recall data for the G80.

I didn't find a thread framed specifically as a one-year ownership review. The closest matches are owner posts scattered across several CT5 threads. They lean toward problems, with some long-term praise.

**Complaints**
- The most detailed negative account is a thread where a buyer traded a certified 2020 CT5 for a new 2025 model. The first car logged fewer than 4,500 miles in about 11 months and needed repeated dealer visits for a fuel module, a timing cover oil leak, a seat belt receptacle, exhaust, and brakes (I drove this for a total of only 4,306 miles in 11 months. During that time, it went to the dealer multiple times for issues like, fuel module replacement, timing cover oil leak, seat belt receptacle, exhaust and brakes.).
- The replacement fared no better. Its SuperCruise feature didn't work, and GM bought back the car and gave the owner an identical replacement after about four weeks. That owner said they ended up liking the car but not the process (It was quite the process and took about 4 weeks to complete but I finally got into the new one and love the car, just didn't like the process.).
- Another post in the same thread describes a car that developed a check engine light within about two weeks, and the dealer reported the engine had failed (I have owned this 13 days and the car has 649 miles! ... The engine has failed, the mechanic is surprised to made it here.).
- A separate CT5-V owner reported the infotainment screen crashing twice within three weeks of delivery. The dealer said a software update had failed, and warned that it could happen again with over-the-air updates (twice within 3 weeks I've had the Infotainment System Center screen crater; the dealership indicates that this failure will occur again when another over-the-air update is attempted).
- In a Kelley Blue Book owner review sample, a few reviewers wanted more suspension adjustability and a larger trunk, and noted that massage seats weren't available with the four-cylinder (I would like more adjustments available re suspension. c) trunk size d) massage seats not available on 4cyl.).

**Positives**
- A 2020 CT5 Sport owner said the car had many problems until about 35,000 miles. After roughly 16,000 trouble-free miles, a door handle failed and cost $335 to fix. The owner still says they really love the car (I like you had soo...many problems up until about 35,000 miles. I'm at 53,000 now, went about 16,000 miles with no more issues until the outside drivers door handle quit working.).
- A 2023 CT5-V owner at roughly 11,000 km says the car still makes them smile whenever they approach, get in, start it, or accelerate (I have around 11k kms on it and it makes me smile every time I walk up to it, get into it, start it up, or punch it.).
- A CT5-V owner who daily drives it chose it for comfort and fuel economy (I daily my V and got it for comfort and gas milage.).
- Kelley Blue Book's 2026 CT5 owner sample is small, with 12 reviewers, and all of them recommend the car. Reviewers praised comfort and quality most (Among the 12 owners who provided feedback on the 2026 Cadillac CT5 for Kelley Blue Book, consumer sentiment is overwhelmingly positive, with 100% recommending the vehicle.).

**Caveats**
- Forum posts skew toward people with problems, so the complaints are likely overrepresented. The KBB sample is only 12 owners.
- The long-term positive accounts mostly come from earlier CT5 model years, not the 2025 refresh.
- To find a true one-year review, search the CT5 forum for terms like "one year" or "12 months," or sort threads by newest.

### Genesis G80 (RG3)

2. **overall_quality_ownership** is the main pain point:
   - towing incidents at about 4,000 and under 10,000 miles
   - repeated shop stays
   - parts and service delays of up to 5 months
   - dealer-network complaints, including "needs its own dealer network"
3. **adas_parking** is split:
   - Owners report Defects: a driver-attention alert that cannot be switched off, non-working emergency braking, erratic lane control.
   - Press credits the standard ADAS suite against BMW's extra-cost packages.
4. **interior_design_quality, exterior_design, audio_acoustics, space_practicality, equipment_value:**
   - AutoGuide picks the G80 over the 540i on interior, styling, Lexicon audio, rear legroom (38.7 vs 36.5 in) and price.
   - A former 5 Series owner also praises the roomier back seat (`competitor_advantage`).
5. **connectivity_app_digital and equipment_value:**
   - Early cars lacked wireless CarPlay and a wireless charging pad, and owners report CarPlay/Bluetooth bugs.
   - One MY2024 owner notes de-contenting: rear shades and soft-close doors removed.
   - Fuel economy (`range_charging_efficiency`) is mixed. The press notes the 3.5T AWD gets 21 mpg against 26 mpg for the 540i.

### Lexus ES (XZ10)
1. **hmi_infotainment** is the clear weak spot: 9 of 13 records are Difficult to Use and 2 are Defect.
   - Causes: the Remote Touch touchpad, an infotainment system "built for an engineer", non-tactile steering-wheel buttons, a navigation bug and a radio-preset bug.
   - Cars.com says the MY2022 12.3-in touchscreen fixed the main issue.
2. **range_charging_efficiency** (ES 300h 40–44 mpg) and smooth ride (**ride_handling**) are the top Likes.
3. **space_practicality** negatives:
   - tight ingress/egress and headroom
   - limited trunk opening
   - rear seats that do not fold (owner and KBB)
   - a single cupholder
4. **audio_acoustics** is mixed:
   - Quietness and the Mark Levinson system are praised.
   - Defects: wind noise that the dealer could not fix (2020 ES 350) and dead rear speakers/subwoofer (2022 ES 300h).
5. **seats_comfort and powertrain_performance:** owners and press want:
   - rear heated seats and rear climate controls
   - AWD with the V6 (only the ES 250 offers AWD)
   - The F Sport ride is harsher (press). One owner recommends the ES over the 5-Series on price and reliability (`competitor_advantage`; the 5 Series generation is not stated).

### Lexus ES (8th gen, MY2026+)
1. **No owner reviews yet.** Cars.com has 0 reviews and KBB shows one hidden review (2.0/5, comfort 1.0). This is a gap, not a finding.
2. Press criticises **powertrain_performance**: performance is tame, even in the ES 500e. **audio_acoustics:** the hybrid is noisy under hard acceleration.
3. Press praises **climate and hmi_infotainment:**
   - a physical HVAC bar and a roller volume dial
   - a crisper 14-in screen with a home button
   - These matter as a counterpoint to touch-only climate concepts.
4. **space_practicality:** rear legroom is 40.7 in (+1.5 in over XZ10) on a 116.1-in wheelbase. The Executive package adds rear recline, heating, ventilation and massage (F12).
5. **equipment_value:** KBB contrasts the sub-$50k EV ES with the BMW i5 and EQE in the high $60ks (`competitor_advantage`). **interior_design_quality:** the synthetic-suede steering wheel is called odd.

### Cadillac CT5 (MY2020+)
1. The owner sample is overwhelmingly positive: 84 of 94 tier-A records are Likes. Most praised are ride_handling, exterior_design and powertrain_performance (2.0T power, up to 36 mpg). Many of these reviews were written early in ownership (2020–2021).
2. **space_practicality** is the main criticism, from owners and press alike:
   - tight rear seat and rear headroom
   - "cozy" trunk of 11.9 cu ft
   - cramped interior
3. **interior_design_quality** is divided. Some owners praise the materials. Cars.com editors find them less upscale than rivals, and one owner reports smelly imitation leather.
4. **The 2025 refresh** brings a 33-in display, Google built-in and Super Cruise.
   - Cars.com lists the tech and Super Cruise as strengths (adas_parking, hmi_infotainment).
   - One 2025 owner finds the car "too hi-tech" and dislikes the 450-page manual, which is sold for $50.
5. **powertrain_performance:** owners like the 2.0T, but Consumer Reports says the powertrain "lacks polish" and Cars.com calls the base four's acceleration so-so. The only BMW comparison is against the 3 Series (owner cross-shopped it, CT5 judged better), so `comparison` is null.

## Coding conventions and caveats

- **Hybrids:** the schema has no HEV value. Non-plug-in hybrids (ES 300h, ES 350h) are coded `ICE`, and the statement mentions "hybrid". For 8th-gen ES press records that cover both hybrid and EV, `powertrain` is `unknown`. MotorWeek records are `BEV`.
- **Electrified G80:** stored as `model: "G80"` with `powertrain: "BEV"`.
- **feedback_type:** dislikes that are neither broken nor a feature request are coded `Difficult to Use` ("weak performance/dissatisfaction"). In press twin tests, categories the G80 loses are coded `Difficult to Use` + `bmw_advantage`.
- **rating:**
  - Owner reviews: null, because cars.com and KBB show only category sub-scores.
  - Press records: the KBB expert score (e.g. `4.7/5`).
- **model_year:**
  - Taken from the review text where stated.
  - Cars.com G80 and CT5 2020 pages are year-specific, so the page year is used there.
  - KBB pages, and the cars.com `lexus-es_350-2019` and `lexus-es_300h-2021` pages, mix model years. Unstated years are null.
  - All KBB/cars.com ES reviews are MY2019–2025, so XZ10. No 2018 or older ES review was used.
- **comparison:**
  - AutoGuide's G80 records compare against the **previous-generation 5 Series (G30, 2021 540i xDrive)**, not the G60.
  - The KBB G80 owner (R020) compares with an earlier 5 Series.
  - The ES owner (R027) names the "5-Series" without a generation.
  - Treat these as brand-level signals.
- **Excluded reviews:**
  - **G80:** cars.com 2021 "Purchased" (describes an SUV). cars.com 2021 "super sleek" (dated Aug 2020, before RG3 US sales; flagged as suspicious). cars.com 2022 "GREAT CARS!" (two weeks of ownership, no car-specific content). KBB "Brand New 2025 GV70" (wrong model). Forum posts by MHT and ctrcbob (workarounds only).
  - **ES:** KBB "Gmoney" and "Simar" (sweepstakes entries). Thin reviews: "Melody22", "Love Lexus Vehicles" (dealer trade-in dispute), "Mary".
  - **CT5:** cars.com "WORST PURCHASE EVER IT IS A 2009" (appears to describe another car). The "Fairfields…" after-sales rant (garbled). "A nice sized SUV…" (hands-free hatch, so not a CT5). "I have only had it one day". KBB "TC Bla" (collision repair only).
- **Conflicts in sources:**
  - KBB ES trunk: 16.7 vs 13.9 cu ft (2025), and 17.4 / 13.3 / 18.2 cu ft (2026).
  - CT5 Super Cruise: standard per the cars.com MY2025 page, "available" per AutoGuide's 2023 launch news.
  - KBB eG80 Level 2 time: 7 h 22 min vs 9 h.
  - All are noted in the equipment `notes`.
- **Equipment:** many F-ids are `unknown` because manufacturer pages were 403 (cadillac.com, news.gm.com) or text-poor (genesis.com, pressroom.lexus.com).
  - Most equipment is tier B, from KBB, Cars.com and MotorWeek.
  - Only the Genesis rows are tier C (genesis.com, MY2027 page, which also shows AWD standard and Bang & Olufsen audio replacing Lexicon).
- **Owner sample size:** small per model (20–26 reviews). Cars.com and KBB samples skew toward early-ownership enthusiasm (CT5, ES 300h) and toward reliability complaints (G80). Compare theme shares, not counts.
- **WebFetch output is a model-written summary.** Records are built only from per-review listings. Paraphrases follow the summary, and short quotes are those the summary placed in quotation marks.

   - Owners report Defects: a driver-attention alert that cannot be switched off, non-working emergency braking, erratic lane control.
   - Press credits the standard ADAS suite against BMW's extra-cost packages.
4. **interior_design_quality, exterior_design, audio_acoustics, space_practicality, equipment_value:**
   - AutoGuide picks the G80 over the 540i on interior, styling, Lexicon audio, rear legroom (38.7 vs 36.5 in) and price.
   - A former 5 Series owner also praises the roomier back seat (`competitor_advantage`).
5. **connectivity_app_digital and equipment_value:**
   - Early cars lacked wireless CarPlay and a wireless charging pad, and owners report CarPlay/Bluetooth bugs.
   - One MY2024 owner notes de-contenting: rear shades and soft-close doors removed.
   - Fuel economy (`range_charging_efficiency`) is mixed. The press notes the 3.5T AWD gets 21 mpg against 26 mpg for the 540i.

### Lexus ES (XZ10)
1. **hmi_infotainment** is the clear weak spot: 9 of 13 records are Difficult to Use and 2 are Defect.
   - Causes: the Remote Touch touchpad, an infotainment system "built for an engineer", non-tactile steering-wheel buttons, a navigation bug and a radio-preset bug.
   - Cars.com says the MY2022 12.3-in touchscreen fixed the main issue.
2. **range_charging_efficiency** (ES 300h 40–44 mpg) and smooth ride (**ride_handling**) are the top Likes.
3. **space_practicality** negatives:
   - tight ingress/egress and headroom
   - limited trunk opening
   - rear seats that do not fold (owner and KBB)
   - a single cupholder
4. **audio_acoustics** is mixed:
   - Quietness and the Mark Levinson system are praised.
   - Defects: wind noise that the dealer could not fix (2020 ES 350) and dead rear speakers/subwoofer (2022 ES 300h).
5. **seats_comfort and powertrain_performance:** owners and press want:
   - rear heated seats and rear climate controls
   - AWD with the V6 (only the ES 250 offers AWD)
   - The F Sport ride is harsher (press). One owner recommends the ES over the 5-Series on price and reliability (`competitor_advantage`; the 5 Series generation is not stated).

### Lexus ES (8th gen, MY2026+)
1. **No owner reviews yet.** Cars.com has 0 reviews and KBB shows one hidden review (2.0/5, comfort 1.0). This is a gap, not a finding.
2. Press criticises **powertrain_performance**: performance is tame, even in the ES 500e. **audio_acoustics:** the hybrid is noisy under hard acceleration.
3. Press praises **climate and hmi_infotainment:**
   - a physical HVAC bar and a roller volume dial
   - a crisper 14-in screen with a home button
   - These matter as a counterpoint to touch-only climate concepts.
4. **space_practicality:** rear legroom is 40.7 in (+1.5 in over XZ10) on a 116.1-in wheelbase. The Executive package adds rear recline, heating, ventilation and massage (F12).
5. **equipment_value:** KBB contrasts the sub-$50k EV ES with the BMW i5 and EQE in the high $60ks (`competitor_advantage`). **interior_design_quality:** the synthetic-suede steering wheel is called odd.

### Cadillac CT5 (MY2020+)
1. The owner sample is overwhelmingly positive: 84 of 94 tier-A records are Likes. Most praised are ride_handling, exterior_design and powertrain_performance (2.0T power, up to 36 mpg). Many of these reviews were written early in ownership (2020–2021).
2. **space_practicality** is the main criticism, from owners and press alike:
   - tight rear seat and rear headroom
   - "cozy" trunk of 11.9 cu ft
   - cramped interior
3. **interior_design_quality** is divided. Some owners praise the materials. Cars.com editors find them less upscale than rivals, and one owner reports smelly imitation leather.
4. **The 2025 refresh** brings a 33-in display, Google built-in and Super Cruise.
   - Cars.com lists the tech and Super Cruise as strengths (adas_parking, hmi_infotainment).
   - One 2025 owner finds the car "too hi-tech" and dislikes the 450-page manual, which is sold for $50.
5. **powertrain_performance:** owners like the 2.0T, but Consumer Reports says the powertrain "lacks polish" and Cars.com calls the base four's acceleration so-so. The only BMW comparison is against the 3 Series (owner cross-shopped it, CT5 judged better), so `comparison` is null.

## Coding conventions and caveats

- **Hybrids:** the schema has no HEV value. Non-plug-in hybrids (ES 300h, ES 350h) are coded `ICE`, and the statement mentions "hybrid". For 8th-gen ES press records that cover both hybrid and EV, `powertrain` is `unknown`. MotorWeek records are `BEV`.
- **Electrified G80:** stored as `model: "G80"` with `powertrain: "BEV"`.
- **feedback_type:** dislikes that are neither broken nor a feature request are coded `Difficult to Use` ("weak performance/dissatisfaction"). In press twin tests, categories the G80 loses are coded `Difficult to Use` + `bmw_advantage`.
- **rating:**
  - Owner reviews: null, because cars.com and KBB show only category sub-scores.
  - Press records: the KBB expert score (e.g. `4.7/5`).
- **model_year:**
  - Taken from the review text where stated.
  - Cars.com G80 and CT5 2020 pages are year-specific, so the page year is used there.
  - KBB pages, and the cars.com `lexus-es_350-2019` and `lexus-es_300h-2021` pages, mix model years. Unstated years are null.
  - All KBB/cars.com ES reviews are MY2019–2025, so XZ10. No 2018 or older ES review was used.
- **comparison:**
  - AutoGuide's G80 records compare against the **previous-generation 5 Series (G30, 2021 540i xDrive)**, not the G60.
  - The KBB G80 owner (R020) compares with an earlier 5 Series.
  - The ES owner (R027) names the "5-Series" without a generation.
  - Treat these as brand-level signals.
- **Excluded reviews:**
  - **G80:** cars.com 2021 "Purchased" (describes an SUV). cars.com 2021 "super sleek" (dated Aug 2020, before RG3 US sales; flagged as suspicious). cars.com 2022 "GREAT CARS!" (two weeks of ownership, no car-specific content). KBB "Brand New 2025 GV70" (wrong model). Forum posts by MHT and ctrcbob (workarounds only).
  - **ES:** KBB "Gmoney" and "Simar" (sweepstakes entries). Thin reviews: "Melody22", "Love Lexus Vehicles" (dealer trade-in dispute), "Mary".
  - **CT5:** cars.com "WORST PURCHASE EVER IT IS A 2009" (appears to describe another car). The "Fairfields…" after-sales rant (garbled). "A nice sized SUV…" (hands-free hatch, so not a CT5). "I have only had it one day". KBB "TC Bla" (collision repair only).
- **Conflicts in sources:**
  - KBB ES trunk: 16.7 vs 13.9 cu ft (2025), and 17.4 / 13.3 / 18.2 cu ft (2026).
  - CT5 Super Cruise: standard per the cars.com MY2025 page, "available" per AutoGuide's 2023 launch news.
  - KBB eG80 Level 2 time: 7 h 22 min vs 9 h.
  - All are noted in the equipment `notes`.
- **Equipment:** many F-ids are `unknown` because manufacturer pages were 403 (cadillac.com, news.gm.com) or text-poor (genesis.com, pressroom.lexus.com).
  - Most equipment is tier B, from KBB, Cars.com and MotorWeek.
  - Only the Genesis rows are tier C (genesis.com, MY2027 page, which also shows AWD standard and Bang & Olufsen audio replacing Lexicon).
- **Owner sample size:** small per model (20–26 reviews). Cars.com and KBB samples skew toward early-ownership enthusiasm (CT5, ES 300h) and toward reliability complaints (G80). Compare theme shares, not counts.
- **WebFetch output is a model-written summary.** Records are built only from per-review listings. Paraphrases follow the summary, and short quotes are those the summary placed in quotation marks.

input.message:
I covered all four models: the G80, the 7th-gen ES, the 8th-gen ES (on sale in the US as MY2026, so it is a separate model) and the CT5. All 440 records pass my schema validator, and every record cites a URL I fetched myself. I used 40 of the ~45 fetches and 9 web searches. I ran no git and changed no other repo files.

Files are in competitors/raw/:
- us_premium_others.jsonl
- us_premium_others.log.md

**Record counts** (unique reviews/posts in brackets):

| Model | Generation label | Competitor | Owner records | Press records | Equipment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Genesis G80 incl. Electrified G80 | RG3 | 1 | 80 review (20) + 11 forum (3) | 28 (2) | 20 |
| Lexus ES, 7th gen | XZ10 | 1 | 99 review (25) | 18 (2) | 20 |
| Lexus ES, 8th gen | 8th gen (MY2026+) | 1 | 0 – none published yet | 14 (2) | 20 |
| Cadillac CT5 | 1st gen (MY2020+) | 1 | 94 review (26) | 12 (2) | 20 |

Every model has a row for each of F01–F20; many are `unknown`. No fetched page states a generation code for the 8th-gen ES or the CT5, so those labels are descriptive rather than invented. The Electrified G80 is stored as model G80 with powertrain BEV.

**Sources**
- **Worked:**
  - cars.com consumer reviews. The Lexus pages only work under the `lexus-es_350-YYYY` / `lexus-es_300h-YYYY` slugs.
  - kbb.com consumer reviews and expert reviews.
  - The AutoGuide G80 vs BMW 5 Series twin test.
  - The cars.com 2022 ES article and the cars.com CT5 2025 research page.
  - MotorWeek (2026 ES), genesis.com, the AutoGuide CT5 news piece, and the genesisowners.com forum.
  - Consumer Reports gave only its free visible text.
- **Failed:**
  - caranddriver.com and motortrend.com: the tool cannot fetch either domain.
  - 403: thecarconnection, autoblog, cadillac.com, news.gm.com.
  - usnews: timed out.
  - cadillacforums.com redirects to a paid bot gateway (tollbit), which I did not follow.
  - Empty: cars.com G80 2024, cars.com 2026 ES 350h (0 reviews), and pressroom.lexus.com (no specs in the first 100k characters).
  - Edmunds was not tried because it is known to be blocked.

**Top 3 findings**
1. **The ES infotainment is its weakest area, while the new ES fixes it with physical controls.** 11 of 13 ES XZ10 infotainment records are negative (touchpad, complex menus, non-tactile buttons). Press for the 8th-gen ES praises its physical climate bar and volume dial. KBB notes the EV ES starts under $50k against the high $60ks for the i5.
2. **G80 owners praise comfort and design but complain about reliability and dealers.** Owners report tow-ins at around 4–10k miles, parts delays of up to 5 months, and driver-assistance defects (an attention alert that cannot be switched off, erratic lane control). In the AutoGuide twin test the G80 beats the previous-generation 540i (G30) on interior, styling, audio, rear legroom (38.7 vs 36.5 in), standard driver assistance and price. The BMW wins on agility, steering, seats and fuel economy.
3. **CT5 owners are very positive except about space.** 79 of 94 owner records are Likes. The main criticism from owners and press alike is the tight rear seat, rear headroom and the 11.9 cu ft trunk. The 2025 refresh (33-inch screen, Super Cruise) is praised by press, but one owner finds it "too hi-tech".

**Anything suspicious**
- **Scratchpad collision:** early on I wrote fetched_ok.txt and validate.py at the shared scratchpad root, which another agent (the Tesla one) was also using. I may have overwritten its files before it rewrote them. I then moved my files to scratchpad/us_premium_others/ and did not touch the root files again; that agent should check its copies.
- **BMW comparisons are mostly not against the G60.** The AutoGuide G80 records compare with the G30, and one G80 owner compares with an earlier 5 Series. One ES owner names the "5-Series" without a generation, and the CT5's only BMW mention is the 3 Series (stored with comparison null).
- **Model years on mixed pages:** KBB appears to pool reviews per generation, so reviews with no stated year are treated as current-generation. The cars.com ES page's pooling is not verified, and one G80 review (R014) cannot be confirmed as RG3 from its own text.
- **Excluded as unreliable:** a G80 review dated before US sales began, two reviews describing SUVs, a "2009" CT5 review, a GV70 review, and sweepstakes entries. All are listed in the log.
- **Conflicting source data:** ES trunk volume differs within the same KBB page, and CT5 Super Cruise is listed as standard by cars.com but "available" by AutoGuide. Both are flagged in the equipment notes.
- **No 8th-gen ES owner voice yet:** the only KBB review is hidden (2.0/5).
